messages:
Maria G: heads up - ran into a weird regression when converting an HF jinja chat_template for onboarding a new model. small change but big eval impact :confused:
Zach H: brief details?
Maria G: the original jinja uses leading newlines inside blocks and relies on the tokenizer's add_prefix_space behavior. our converter stripped a leading whitespace on the first user message, so tokenization shifted.
Lauren P: that sounds like the classic prefix-space issue. which tokenizer and model?
Maria G: model: hf/small-chat-xx (onboard candidate). tokenizer had `add_prefix_space=true` in HF config but our conversion didn't preserve it. quantized 4-bit build (bitsandbytes) shows amplified behavior — answers become truncated and start repeating.
Sam T: do you have a minimal repro?
Maria G: yep, snippet below. original jinja:
```
{% set msg = user_input %}
{{system}}

User: {{ msg }}
Assistant:
```
converted Redwood prompt we generated:
```
SYSTEM: {{system}}\nUser:{{user_input}}\nAssistant:
```
Notice missing space after `User:` and removed blank line.
Zach H: missing space -> different token boundaries. if tokenizer expects a leading space before words it merges tokens. small change -> different attention / kv split after quantization.
Maria G: exactly. eval-harness results on our chat QA suite: EM dropped 0.79 -> 0.71, rouge-l -4.3. small but consistent across seeds. eval-bot: regression detected on nightly: task=chat_qa, delta_em=-0.08, flagged=true.
eval-bot: [automated] opened ticket REDWOOD-ML-457 for regression, attached diffs and sample mismatches.
Lauren P: immediate repro fix: keep whitespace and explicit sentinel mapping. two options:
1) preserve raw whitespace when rendering jinja (use `{% raw %}` around blocks or ensure converter avoids trim).
2) explicitly set tokenizer feature in converted config: "add_prefix_space": true and map `special_tokens_map` for system/user/assistant markers.
Zach H: also add a unit test: compare HF-rendered tokens vs Redwood-rendered tokens for a few canonical messages. something like:
```
assert hf_tokenizer.encode(hf_rendered) == rw_tokenizer.encode(rw_rendered)
```
We should add that to tests/evals/test_chat_template_tokenization.py.
Sam T: would changing add_prefix_space break other models? need to bump test matrix.
Lauren P: yeah run a matrix across models in the canary stage. for Dedicated customers we should be conservative and fallback to previous conversion if mismatch > threshold.
Maria G: quick workaround pushed to conversion script: preserve leading/trailing blank lines and keep a single space after role labels. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/convert/pull/129 :eyes:.
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for 2 hosts in us-west, tag=chattemplate-fix-129.
Zach H: follow-up: check quantized kernels too. some of the 4-bit packing expects token alignment; off-by-one token ids can trigger emulation of repeated tokens. worth a micro-benchmark.
Maria G: noted. I'll run the token-alignment microbench and attach results to REDWOOD-ML-457. thanks all :thumbsup:
Lauren P: assign me to the ticket for coordinating canary and evals.
Maria G: assigning Lauren.
Sam T: one more: add a small human-readable example in docs for common jinja pitfalls (leading newline, trimmed blocks, raw blocks). low effort, high ROI.
Maria G: agreed — I'll draft a short section in the onboarding checklist.
